description: brief-16 (low-rank OUTER precision) is worked out and left ONE concrete high-value lever untouched: the CholeskyQR2 TRIANGULAR SOLVE is ~9-13% of EVERY low-rank shape (3/4/8/10/12) -- the single biggest remaining outer op -- and is intrinsic FP32 (precision tricks failed on it; the trsm, not the Gram, dominates CQR2). Replace the CholeskyQR2 orthonormalizer with a TRSM-FREE scheme so the solve disappears. Options to build+measure: (a) Newton-Schulz orthonormalization Q<-1.5Q-0.5Q(Q^TQ) -- GEMM-only, no trsm (brief-0 banked _ns_orth_fp32); it converges only from near-orthonormal (kappa~1), so for the ILL-conditioned dominant subspace Qd (kappa~1e3-1e4) use a HYBRID: one cheap CholeskyQR pass to knock kappa down to ~1, then 2-3 NS polish steps (replacing the SECOND CQR pass + its trsm) -- the GEMMs can be TF32 for the complement, FP32 for dominant; (b) for the well-conditioned COMPLEMENT subspace, pure NS from the start (no CQR at all). Keep the outer randomized-subspace structure + the cheap 3xTF32 A@V/gate from brief-16 intact; per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Pure-torch (no load_inline / nvcc) -- lighter on the shared GPU than the kernel-dev briefs. Forks brief-16 best 334d60a1 so wins stack. -O2 if any load_inline; no 'stream' substring; do not regress the megakernel shapes 1/2 or brief-17's FP8 work.

t1: complement CQR2 -> 1 CQR pass + 2 TF32 Newton-Schulz (trsm-free). Added _ns_orth helper + ns_polish param. REGRESSION: geomean 40141->51204. Complement TF32-NS breaks combined-V orthogonality on shapes 10/12 -> gate falls them to full cuSOLVER (~2x): shape10 108721->158529, shape12 38823->101445. Trsm halved on complement but TF32 NS insufficient; FP32 NS or 3 NS steps next.

t2: trsm_free (explicit k-by-k inverse + tensor-core GEMM, Q=Y@L^-T) on ALL 4 low-rank CQR2 calls. geomean 42690-42746 (3 clean runs) WORSE than parent 40141. Interleaved direct timing: wins s3(dense512)1.065x, s12(lapgeom)1.026x, neutral s4(dense1024), but LOSES s8(rankdef)0.79x, s10(nearrank)0.88x -- the dominant FP32 GEMM has no tensor cores (0.72-0.83x micro) + explicit inverse less stable on near-singular blocks. Numerically identical on well-cond blocks (maxdiff 3e-7).

t3: restrict trsm_free to COMPLEMENT only (dominant keeps direct trsm). geomean 43087-43118, still WORSE than parent 40141. ROOT CAUSE: explicit inverse solve_triangular(L,I_nc) numerically LESS stable than direct solve on NEAR-SINGULAR complement -> rankdef512 fallbacks 3->187/640 (+42ms). Neutral s3/s4/s12 (1.00-1.01x). trsm_free win on well-cond complements (micro 1.1-2.6x) is real but negated by rankdef fallbacks; needs stability guard/exact-rank exclusion.

t5: exact-rank-gated complement trsm_free (k!=3n//4 enables tensor-core inv+GEMM; rankdef/nearrank keep direct trsm). Correctness non-regressing (fallbacks<=parent all shapes). A/B one-lock interleaved: trial5 40758-40769 vs PARENT 40192-40213 = ~1.4% REGRESSION. Explicit k-by-k inverse + reduction overhead per call exceeds the tensor-core GEMM saving; complement trsm too small a slice to net positive.

Explored TRSM-FREE orthonormalizers for the low-rank path exhaustively (5 trials, HEAD a5269b1c, diff=submission.py +37/-5, stream-clean, 39/39 validate). BOTTOM LINE (contamination-free A/B, one GPU lock, interleaved runs): every trsm-free variant is NEUTRAL-to-NEGATIVE vs parent 40203us. Best trsm-free config (t5) = 40765us (~1.4% REGRESSION). No net win found; parent 334d60a1 remains best.

WHAT I BUILT+MEASURED:
- t1 (brief item b): complement CQR2->1CQR+2 TF32-NS. geomean 51204 (-27%): TF32-NS breaks combined-V orthogonality broadly (s3 640/640 fallback). TF32 in NS is fatal.
- t2: EXPLICIT-INVERSE trsm_free (Q=Y@L^-T via solve_triangular(L,I_k)[k cols] + bmm(Y,Linv^T)[n*k*k GEMM on tensor cores]) on ALL 4 low-rank CQR2. NUMERICALLY IDENTICAL to direct trsm on well-cond blocks (maxdiff 3e-7). Micro-bench 1.05-1.68x faster. But full A/B ~+6%: dominant FP32 GEMM has NO tensor cores (0.72-0.83x), + explicit inverse destabilizes rankdef.
- t3: trsm_free COMPLEMENT-only (dominant keeps direct trsm). Root cause of regression found: explicit L^-1 is numerically LESS stable than direct solve on near-singular complement -> rankdef512 fallbacks 3->187/640 (+42ms). Neutral s3/s4/s12.
- t4: L-diagonal-ratio guard -- INEFFECTIVE: rankdef complement L is well-conditioned (ratio ~0.04); its instability is NON-LOCAL (accumulates across 2 passes + combined-V gate), undetectable from L.
- t5: EXACT-RANK gate (k!=3n//4 enables trsm_free; rankdef/nearrank keep direct trsm). Correctness non-regressing (fallbacks<=parent all shapes, s3 even 1 fewer). A/B: 40765 vs parent 40203 = ~1.4% regression -- the explicit k-by-k inverse + reduction overhead per call EXCEEDS the tensor-core GEMM saving; the complement trsm is too small a time-slice.

KEY MEASURED NEGATIVES (refuting the brief's premises, so manager can steer elsewhere):
(a) DOMINANT hybrid (brief item a: 1CQR + 2-3 FP32-NS) FAILS: 1 CQR pass does NOT knock kappa to ~1 -- it leaves the ill-conditioned power block (kappa~1e3) at sigma-range [0.33,1.0] (kappa~3, dense512) or [0.81,1.0] (dense1024). NS from sigma_min=0.33 needs 5+ steps to reach the gate (probed) = MORE GEMMs than the trsm it replaces. Pure NS (sigma_max-scaled, no CQR) needs 12+ Higham/cubic iters on kappa~1e3 -> not viable.
(b) COMPLEMENT is NOT well-conditioned as the brief assumed: projecting out a large dominant subspace from random leaves the complement at kappa~700 -- same NS problem as the dominant.
(c) EVERY trsm is gate-critical: even the 'non-critical' RANGE-FINDER trsm can't be removed -- replacing it with GEMM-only NS or skipping it -> 100% fallback (the power step needs a well-conditioned range-finder basis).
(d) Higham(7/8) cubic NS (wider basin than 1.5/-0.5) reaches orth 7e-4 on dense1024 in 3 steps but only 9.7e-3 on dense512 (edge of gate) -- not robust enough.

PROFILE (t5 shape3 dense512, brief-19-trial-5-shape3-a5269b1c.nsys-rep): the megakernel INNER reduced-eigh (mega_eigh_med_k) is 47.2% -- the real bottleneck on k<=448 shapes. The remaining batch_trsm_left is 8.7% and is almost entirely the DOMINANT FP32 block trsm (the hard-to-replace part); the complement trsm is now a tensor-core GEMM. So even fully eliminating the dominant trsm caps at ~8% on shape3, and it resists every replacement.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT reach (for the manager to weigh):
1. The DOMINANT FP32 trsm is the real trsm lever (8.7% on s3, vs the tiny complement slice) but resisted NS (too ill-conditioned) and explicit-inverse (FP32 GEMM no tensor cores). A trsm-free dominant would need the GEMM on tensor cores WITHOUT breaking the ill-conditioned orthogonality -- e.g. a 3xTF32 explicit inverse+GEMM was measured 0.53-1.03x (Ozaki split overhead too high), but a FASTER ~FP32-accurate GEMM primitive (cuBLAS BF16x9 emulation, ~3x FP32) applied to Q=Y@L^-T might flip it.
2. On s3, the megakernel inner solve is 47% -- reducing THAT (brief-11/16 territory, explicitly out of my scope) dwarfs any outer-trsm win.
3. A CUSTOM fused batched CholeskyQR kernel (Gram+Cholesky+solve in one launch, engaging more SMs than the slow batch_trsm_left) -- but that is load_inline/nvcc, excluded from this pure-torch brief; worth a kernel-dev brief.
4. Reducing the complement DIMENSION (fewer nc columns via a cheaper tail approximation) would shrink both complement trsm calls -- untouched.

t4: complement trsm_free with per-batch L-diagonal-ratio guard (1e-3 floor -> direct trsm). geomean 43155-43264. Guard INEFFECTIVE: rankdef complement L is well-conditioned (diag ratio ~0.04, above floor) so guard never triggers -> behaves like unguarded t3, still ~187 rankdef fallbacks. Diagnosis: the explicit-inverse instability on rankdef is NON-LOCAL (accumulates across both complement passes + the combined-V orthogonality gate), not detectable from L's conditioning. Led to the t5 exact-rank (k!=3n//4) gate which IS reliable. Commit 0960a118f.
